title: Smallest Upright Rectangle From Points
statement:
You get a list of distinct points on a grid, points[i] = [x, y]. Pick four of them that are the corners of a rectangle whose sides run parallel to the x and y axes.

Return the smallest area such a rectangle can have. If no four points form one, return 0. Tilted rectangles do not count.

examples.why: Three rectangles exist, with x-ranges 0–2, 2–5 and 0–5 and height 3. The narrowest one is 2 × 3.
The fourth point is at x = 3, not 4, so the corners never close.
These four points form a square, but it is tilted 45°.

hints: Four nested loops over 500 points is far too slow. An upright rectangle is fixed by just two of its corners. Which two?
Two opposite corners (x1, y1) and (x2, y2), with x1 ≠ x2 and y1 ≠ y2, fix the other two: (x1, y2) and (x2, y1).
Put every point in a hash set. For every pair of points that could be a diagonal, check the other two corners in O(1) and keep the smallest area.

explain.intuition:
An axis-parallel rectangle is completely fixed by one diagonal. If (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) are opposite corners, the other two corners must be exactly (x1, y2) and (x2, y1). So instead of choosing four points, choose two, and look up the other two.

A hash set of points makes the lookup O(1), so the whole search is O(n²) pairs. Encode a point as one number such as x · 40001 + y so the set compares values, not array references, which in JavaScript would never match.
steps: Put every point into a set, encoded as x · 40001 + y.
For every pair i < j with different x and different y, treat them as a diagonal.
If both (x1, y2) and (x2, y1) are in the set, update the best area with |x1 − x2| · |y1 − y2|.
Return the best area, or 0 if none was found.
pitfalls: Putting [x, y] arrays in a JavaScript Set. Arrays compare by reference, so every lookup fails.
Accepting pairs that share an x or a y. They are a side, not a diagonal, and give area 0.
Returning Infinity (or the initial sentinel) instead of 0 when no rectangle exists.

solutions.title: Diagonal pairs with a linear scan
solutions.idea: Try every pair as a diagonal and scan the whole list for the other two corners.

solutions.title: Hash set of points, check each diagonal
solutions.idea: Two opposite corners fix the other two. Look them up in a set of encoded points.

followups: Group points by x and, for each pair of y values, remember the last x where both appeared. Why can that beat O(n²) on some inputs?
Allow tilted rectangles too. What property of the two diagonals do you hash?
